clue.text: Neanderthal on the loose with saw

parts.note: an escaped animal on the loose is out
to see someone is to date them, so saw gives dated

explanation.surface: A caveman runs wild brandishing a saw.
explanation.definitionFit: Neanderthal is used figuratively for old-fashioned, primitive attitudes, which are behind the times.

clue.text: 1 across lot had broken

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 1 across, meaning out of date

indicators.note: the words lot had are broken up and put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A batch of goods arrived broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something stale and no longer fashionable, the same sense as out of date.

clue.text: A temple is used for photographic technique

indicators.note: used in the sense of worn or knocked about, so the letters of a temple is are reshaped

explanation.surface: A temple serves as the subject of a photographer's special technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lapse photography shoots frames at long intervals so slow change looks fast when played back.

clue.text: Principal gone from school, might have been fired?

indicators.note: the principal, or leading, letter has gone from the school's name, so it is dropped

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A headteacher has left the school, perhaps because they were sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests the sacked principal, but it is the definition: an arrow is shot, or fired, from a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a projectile that is shot from a bow, loosely said to be fired.

clue.text: Jewellery item slipping, article secured

indicators.note: the slipping word has the article secured within it

parts.note: slipping up is erring, making a mistake
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery keeps slipping until an item is fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring is an ornament worn on the ear lobe, a common piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Damage one married couple

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Harm comes to a single married couple.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or harm, a verb synonym of damage.

clue.text: Youngster with case for diamonds, say?

parts.note: a minor is a person under adult age
a suit is a case brought in a court of law

explanation.surface: A child with a briefcase suited to carrying gems.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, diamonds and clubs are the minor suits, scoring less than hearts and spades; 'say' marks diamonds as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds is an example of the lower-ranking pair of card suits in bridge scoring.

clue.text: A dessert served up, cold

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a fool is a pudding of fruit purée folded into cream

explanation.surface: A pudding is brought out chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British dessert of puréed fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof describes someone distant and unfriendly in manner, the figurative sense of cold.

clue.text: Oil processor on, very hot, nitrogen going in

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: the nitrogen symbol goes in the word for very hot

parts.note: fiery means very hot
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: An oil plant keeps running extremely hot as nitrogen is pumped in.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is an industrial plant where crude oil is purified into fuels.

clue.text: Excellent rolls coated with nuts made for something sweet

indicators.note: the reversed word is coated with the rearranged letters around it
nuts means crazy, so the letters of made are rearranged
rolls over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: rare can mean unusually fine or excellent

explanation.surface: Fine bread rolls with a nut coating were baked as a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent' is rare as in a rare talent; the surface makes 'rolls' bread and 'nuts' a coating, but both are signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a light brown cane sugar, so it is literally a sweet substance.

clue.text: Extraordinary example, bit short?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something unique that happens only once
second meaning: read literally, short by one

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words: being one off is falling one short.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is a unique, unrepeated instance, while one off literally means a single unit missing.

clue.text: Unfeeling heart filled with venom, ultimately

indicators.note: the heart word is filled with that letter

parts.note: the nub is the heart or core of something

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of venom

explanation.surface: A cold heart full of spite at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means deprived of sensation, so without feeling.

clue.text: A learner down for permit

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British car
down as in low in spirits

explanation.surface: A sad learner driver going for their permit.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow is to let something happen, a straight synonym of the verb permit.

clue.text: Drug required if one has burp that's windy

indicators.note: windy suggests the letters are blown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Medicine is needed when a person keeps belching.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common over-the-counter painkiller, an anti-inflammatory medicine.

clue.text: Careful extracting a coil

indicators.note: extracting means the letter a is pulled out of the word

parts.note: sparing means careful or economical

explanation.surface: Be careful when pulling a coil out of a mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a helix of wire, a coil that stores energy when compressed.

clue.text: I get closer to home, with considerable commitment

parts.note: nearer, so near in the sense of closer to
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone moving nearer home feels a deep sense of dedication.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something in earnest is to do it seriously and sincerely, with real commitment.

clue.text: Cry, finding part of a whale

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the thick fat layer of a whale

explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to sob, and blubber is also the insulating fat under a whale's skin.

clue.text: Mark supports strike

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
to lash is to strike with a whip

explanation.surface: Mark backs a walkout by the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; it is the definition, a typed symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A backslash is the typographical symbol slanting from top left to bottom right.

clue.text: Painter, perhaps, with some light colours initially filling in bridge

indicators.note: the light and letter are filling in the gap within the bridge word

parts.note: a span is a bridge, or the stretch it crosses
a ray is a beam, some light

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of colours

explanation.surface: An artist adds light colours to a painting of a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray can is an aerosol used to apply paint, so it is something that paints.

clue.text: Something wrapped up here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gift, which is usually wrapped
second meaning: in attendance, not absent

explanation.definitionFit: A present is a wrapped gift, and to be present is to be in attendance.

clue.text: Drawer as yet unopened

indicators.note: unopened says the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: still means as yet, up to now

explanation.surface: A drawer that has not yet been opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A till is the cash drawer of a shop register.

clue.text: Routine in hospital fuelling criticism

indicators.note: the hospital letter goes into the criticism word, feeding it from inside

parts.note: stick is informal British for harsh criticism
H is the map symbol for a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital's routine is stoking complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking stick is British slang for being criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: A shtick is a performer's familiar act or comic routine.

clue.text: Tail of yellow in yellowish bird

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the yellowish word

parts.note: sallow describes a sickly yellowish complexion

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A yellow-tailed bird of a yellowish colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallow is a fork-tailed migratory songbird.

clue.text: Snake pretty empty, but heading for nest

indicators.note: empty means the inside of pretty is removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: tho is short for though, meaning but

indicators.note: the heading of nest is its first letter

explanation.surface: A snake slithers off, rather aimless, but heading for its nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The python is a large constricting snake.

clue.text: A ritual as barbaric somewhere in the southern hemisphere

indicators.note: barbaric suggests savage disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A barbaric ritual practised somewhere south of the equator.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a country and continent lying entirely below the equator.

clue.text: Faculty, horrible mess

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sense of vision
second meaning: as in you look a ..., something unsightly

explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses, and a sight is also an informal word for an untidy or ugly appearance.

clue.text: Some word is hyphenated ñ good- looking?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A self-referential clue: one word is printed with a hyphen, then a word for attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray ñ is a garbled dash in the source text, and good-looking itself is split by a hyphen, echoing the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is informal British slang for attractive, describing a handsome person.

clue.text: Leading journalist turned over storehouse

indicators.note: turned over means the words are read backwards

parts.note: top means leading or foremost
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A leading reporter overturned a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse or storage place for goods.

clue.text: Little bird that would make an impression, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken and the sound is what counts

parts.note: a signet ring is pressed into wax to make an impression

explanation.surface: A small bird tries to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, so a little bird in age.

clue.text: Make-up, small amount applied carelessly

parts.note: slap is British theatre slang for make-up
a dash is a small amount, as of milk

explanation.surface: A dab of make-up, slapped on without care.
explanation.walkthrough: Slap is British slang for greasepaint or cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash means hastily and without care, as an adverb as well as an adjective.

clue.text: No place for art record

parts.note: the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain

explanation.surface: No gallery is set aside for an artwork record.
explanation.walkthrough: TATE is the London art gallery group, including Tate Modern.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to write down, especially music, in a system of symbols.

clue.text: Two chins wobbling, set off

indicators.note: wobbling chins shake the letters into a different order

explanation.surface: A double chin jiggles as its owner starts moving.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch on a device is to activate or set it going.
